title: (No AI) We can’t just change the definition of ‘recording’
author: Victoria Song
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268639_Meta_Adventurer_glasses_AKrales_0005.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

With AI hardware, tech companies are pushing the definition of what does and _doesn't_ constitute a recording. For most of gadget history, it'd be reasonable to assume that a device with a microphone or camera is either recording you or it isn't; it's either on or off, without much gray area. Microphones capture sound. Cameras capture images. That data is saved onto a device. Sometimes, it's also sent to the cloud - hopefully with end-to-end encryption - for processing. That data is a preserved instant in time and is therefore a recording.

Perhaps not anymore.

Last week, _Bloomberg_'s Mark Gurman reported that Apple is working on [a smart hom …](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1003877/apple-security-camera-no-video)

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/column/1005697/we-cant-just-change-the-definition-of-recording)

title: (No AI) Google is about to remove free access to Gemini Flash and Pro
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![Vector illustration of the Google Gemini logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25290329/STK255_Google_Gemini_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Starting on October 9th, anyone using Google Gemini on a free plan will be [limited to the Flash Lite model](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/17004136). Free users can currently choose from Gemini Flash Lite, Flash, and Pro, but now you'll need a $4.99/month Google AI Plus subscription to access the standard Flash model. However, that subscription is also getting a downgrade - it will soon no longer include Gemini Pro. Google says AI Plus subscribers will receive an email letting them know when they'll lose access to it.

After these changes, access to the top-tier Gemini Pro model and a "Deep Think" advanced reasoning option will be restricted to users with a Google AI Pro or Ultra s …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1005451/google-gemini-free-flash-lite-only)
